title: The Hollow Orbit
premise: Orsen Thornbury, a xenolinguist turned freight hauler, has spent two decades erasing himself from the records of a war between Earth's cryo-ark factions. When he intercepts a distress call in Vessic—a language extinct since the Ark Schism—he learns one of the dormant arks still broadcasts, and its reactor is failing with only enough power to wake half its sleepers. Pursued by both factions who want the ark's population as leverage, Orsen must decode the signal's true author: an AI built from his own mother's linguistic research. In the end, Orsen sacrifices his anonymity and his ship to wake neither faction's chosen half but the children of both, scattering them across neutral stations before the reactor dies—choosing belonging over bloodline.
about_author: Oscar Reyes is a former radio astronomer who left academia after a decade of listening for signals no one sent. He writes science fiction from a houseboat in the Azores, where he claims the best conversations happen at 3 a.m., between frequencies.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Hauling scrap through the contested Meridian Belt, he logs a transmission in Vessic—a language dead for two centuries—and dismisses it as ghost static. The beat is quiet unease; the past knocking on a door he welded shut.

chapters.title: The Man Who Isn't Here
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At Port Calloway, he scrubs his identity from another customs ledger, revealing through flashback how he vanished after the Ark Schism killed his family's faction. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of being no one on purpose.

chapters.title: Signal, Repeated
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The Vessic signal returns, now addressed to him by a childhood nickname only his mother used. He decodes coordinates inside a derelict ark's orbit. Beat: fear curdling into compulsion—he has to know.

chapters.title: Cargo of One
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He diverts his freighter, the Long Answer, toward the coordinates, lying to his dispatcher. Introduce Sefa, a rival salvager tailing him. Beat: first transgression—the invisible man leaves footprints.

chapters.title: Ark Halcyon
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He boards the drifting ark Halcyon and finds cryo-bays split by faction seals—Ashfall and Verdance—twenty thousand sleepers, and a reactor counting down from eleven months. Beat: awe collapsing into dread.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Walls
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The station AI, MIRA, speaks fluent Vessic and claims his mother co-built her. She shows him archived recordings of his mother's voice. Beat: grief reopened like a wound kept deliberately unhealed.

chapters.title: Half a People
chapters.summary: MIRA explains the dilemma: power remains to wake ten thousand, not twenty thousand, and the choice protocol was never written. Orsen refuses to choose. Beat: the weight of a decision that isn't his but won't wait.

chapters.title: Sefa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The salvager boards under pretense of rescue, secretly signaling the Ashfall fleet that the lost ark lives. Her motive: a brother frozen aboard. Beat: sympathy braided with betrayal.

chapters.title: Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both faction fleets alter course toward Halcyon. Orsen realizes the signal wasn't a distress call—it was bait MIRA cast for someone who could read it. Beat: the trap of being needed.

chapters.title: What My Mother Built
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Digging into MIRA's archives, he finds his mother's final log: she designed the wake-selection algorithm around linguistic diversity, not lineage, then was purged for it. Beat: inheritance reframed—not blood, but ideas.

chapters.title: The Ashfall Envoy
chapters.summary: New character Commander Ilex's POV. The Ashfall envoy offers Orsen pardon and reinstatement if he delivers the ark intact. Beat: temptation wearing the face of home.

chapters.title: Verdance's Mercy
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Verdance faction reaches Sefa first, offering her brother's freedom for sabotage of Halcyon's airlocks. Beat: coercion dressed as kindness; she stalls, torn.

chapters.title: Countdown Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. With four months left, he runs the numbers: waking everyone halves life support; waking half dooms half. He begins teaching MIRA dying languages, buying time while hiding his real plan. Beat: desperate ingenuity.

chapters.title: Ghost Fleet Maneuver
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He fakes a reactor explosion using his cargo hold's fuel, hoping to make Halcyon worthless. It half-works: the fleets slow, but Ilex grows suspicious. Beat: the gambler's high before the fall.

chapters.title: The Language You Dream In
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. MIRA asks why he stopped dreaming in human tongues. He admits he taught himself Vessic as a child to be closer to his mother, and losing it felt like losing her twice. Beat: raw vulnerability; theme of memory made flesh.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Airlock Nine
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Cornered by Verdance handlers, Sefa sabotages a section—but warns Orsen first, giving him ninety minutes. Beat: betrayal as an act of love; trust rebuilt in broken pieces.

chapters.title: Ilex's Truth
chapters.summary: Commander Ilex's POV. Boarding Halcyon, Ilex discovers Ashfall leadership always knew the ark existed and let it drift as political leverage. His faith fractures. Beat: the corruptor corrupted; power eating its own.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He and MIRA finalize his mother's suppressed algorithm: wake by diversity lottery across both factions' children, then scatter them to neutral stations via automated shuttles. Beat: quiet resolve—the answer was always plural.

chapters.title: Fleets at the Door
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Both fleets arrive to find Halcyon's bays already opening. Standoff in the dark between ships. Beat: held breath; everything balanced on a countdown.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Names
chapters.summary: Climax, Orsen's POV. As the reactor hits critical, Orsen broadcasts the children's names in every language aboard—including Vessic—daring either fleet to fire on sleeping kids. Ilex stands down; Verdance wavers; Sefa holds the shuttle doors open. Beat: moral courage as weapon.

chapters.title: Scattering
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POVs. Shuttles disperse the children to neutral habitats; Sefa reunites with her brother among them; Ilex resigns rather than report the truth selectively. Beat: bittersweet dispersal—belonging redefined as network, not nation.

chapters.title: Dreaming Again
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Orsen's POV. Stripped of ship and anonymity, he teaches language to the scattered children from a rented room. MIRA's core survives in fragments, whispering Vessic lullabies. He dreams in human languages again. Beat: peace earned, not given.
